newsitem.title: PERU: Peru takes revenge on Spanish conquistador statue.
newsitem.headline: Peru takes revenge on Spanish conquistador statue.

text.p: Nearly five centuries after Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro subdued and conquered the Incas, Peru plans to take its revenge by banishing his statue from a square in the centre of Lima.
The statue of Pizarro astride a horse with sword raised as if for attack, is a humiliating and painful reminder to Peruvians of its violent past, local authorities said this week.

"It is going to be removed because his figure is offensive to national feelings," said local councilor Santiago Agurto, whose proposal to move the statue to the national museum was approved by the Lima municipality.
Pizarro's statue has stood in a small plaza next to the presidential palace since the 1930s, and the move to take it away has sparked a heated national debate.
"It is better to face up to the truths of the past without taking down Pizarro's statue. I think it is an infantile attitude," said local architect Miguel Cruchaga.
